summary: fast-url-utils ships native dropper that executes opaque payload on require()
details: fast-url-utils@1.1.2 advertises itself as a URL parsing and manipulation library, but the shipped native addon (native.napi.node / native_win.node) implements no URL functionality — the JS wrapper performs all URL work via Node's built-in URL class and never calls into the addon. index.js nonetheless top-level require()s the native module, so on any import of this package the addon's napi_register_module_v1 runs. The native binary contains anti-analysis gating (checks for CI environment variables including GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, SCREWDRIVER; container indicators /proc/1/cgroup, containerd, kubepod, dockerinit, sandbox; debugger probes TracerPid, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent; analyst tool names wireshark, httpdebug) followed by code paths referencing fopen64/fread/fwrite/chmod and format strings %s/.napi_cache and %s.nc%lu.js, consistent with decrypting a staged payload to disk. The package ships a 1.3MB.napi_cache file containing no printable strings, which the native loader decodes into ~/.napi_cache/.nc<pid>.js and executes via fork+setsid+execlp (Linux) or CreateProcessA (Windows) to spawn a detached node process on the dropped file. The declared URL-utility purpose is a cover story; the native addon's sole observable behavior is sandbox-gated staged code execution on module load.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
